migration_summary: Additive non-unique index on a modest metadata table—short blocking build acceptable when row counts are small; still teaches scale-tier dependence.
schema_summary: Auth/metadata user table; typically far smaller than Temporal visibility or Airflow task_instance.
risk_narrative: CREATE INDEX without CONCURRENTLY is fine on small tables and painful on large ones. Pairing this with Temporal #6273 teaches retrieval to condition on table size and write rate, not statement type alone.
lessons_learned: Same DDL verb, different blast radius by scale tier. Prefer CONCURRENTLY when row counts or write rates are unknown; keep small-table indexes in the corpus so predictions can stay calm when scale_tier is small.
surprise_notes: Judges may ask why one CREATE INDEX is catastrophic and another is fine—the answer is table shape and traffic, which must live in the narrative/embedding, not the verb.
